rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samarrāʾī calls these observations guiding signs of the Qur’an’s deliberate, uniquely controlled artistry, while the full inimitability exceeds any description.
rows.anchor: لا نقول: إن هذه هي مواطن الإعجاز، ولا بعض مواطن الإعجاز وإنما هي ملامح ودلائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He presents the Qur’an as descending from the highest assembly through a noble angel, with inexhaustible signs of divine inimitability.
rows.anchor: إن هذا القادم من الملأ الأعلى، والذي نزل به سيدٌ من كبار سادات الملأ الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He imagines Qur’anic admonitions opening a spiritually closed heart and stirring awe and tears, invoking the call to humility and the Qur’an’s ease for remembrance.
rows.anchor: أَلَمْ يَأْنِ لِلَّذِينَ آمنوا أَن تَخْشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ لِذِكْرِ الله وَمَا نَزَلَ مِنَ الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening pairing of humility with turning from idle speech is reinforced throughout al-Mu’minūn: righteous work and haste in good oppose heedlessness, ridicule, rejection, and transgression.
rows.anchor: ولوضع هذه الصفة - أعني الإعراض عن اللغو - بجنب الخشوع له دلالة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Further passages call creation purposeful and affirm that the Qur’an brings truth, completing the surah’s contrast between truth and idle speech or falsehood.
rows.anchor: والعبث هو الباطل، وهو من اللغو واللهو، ووصف الله نفسه بالحق، والحقُّ نقيضُ الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting عن اللغو before معرضون makes avoidance stronger than merely not engaging: they keep away from its presence and sound, and turn away if they hear it.
rows.anchor: فإن قوله: {عَنِ اللغو مُّعْرِضُونَ} أبلغ من (لا يلغون)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominal construction presents turning away from idle speech as an established, enduring quality, consistent with the other traits attributed to the believers.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى أن إعراضهم عن اللغو، وصفٌ ثابت فيهم، وليس شيئاً طارئاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He describes his writing as signs placed along the way, a faint lamp intended to benefit travelers and invite their prayers.
rows.anchor: إنما هي دلائلُ أضعها في الطريق وإشارات وصُوى، وشيء من خافت النورِ في مصباحٍ ناضبِ الزيت

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet counsels Abū Dharr to prepare carefully for the deep sea, travel light over the steep ascent, carry provisions for a long journey, and purify his work before its discerning judge.
rows.anchor: ما أوصى به رسولُ الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صاحبه أبا ذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭā Hā directly addresses Moses, instructs him in worship and prayer, and recalls his life in direct speech; this suits the personal wording I am your Lord, unlike the narrative treatment in al-Qaṣaṣ.
rows.anchor: فإنه لم يذكر توجيهاً له أو إرشاداً لعبادته في النمل، ولا في القصص فلم يأمره بعبادة أو صلاة أو تكليف خاص بشأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Naml’s direct imperative reports God’s exact words and signals honor; al-Qaṣaṣ’s أن ألق describes the meaning of the call without requiring those exact words.
rows.anchor: فقوله: {وَأَلْقِ عَصَاكَ} قولٌ مباشر من رب العزة، وهو دال على التكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite names al-ʿAzīz and al-Ḥakīm signal exclusive perfection, answering Pharaoh’s self-styled might; indefinite forms could allow others to share those qualities.
rows.anchor: فإن فرعونَ حاكمٌ متجبر يرتدي رداء العزة، ألا ترى كيف أقسم السحرةُ بعزته قائلين: {بِعِزَّةِ فِرْعَونَ إِنَّا لَنَحْنُ الغالبون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭā Hā says your Lord because its scene first directs Moses personally to worship and prayer; al-Naml and al-Qaṣaṣ use Lord of the worlds, and al-Naml adds the names al-ʿAzīz al-Ḥakīm.
rows.anchor: أنه في سورة طه كان الخطاب والتوجيه لموسى عليه السلام أولاً فعلّمه وأرشده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the person facing punishment is a criminal desperate to escape, he would sacrifice even his closest loved ones and, in principle, all people for himself.
rows.anchor: والمجرمُ مستعدٌّ لِفعْلِ أيِّ شيء لينجو ولو أن يبدأ بأقرب المُقَرَّبين إليه وأحبهم إلى قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence begins with children because the preceding verse has already mentioned close kin, then expands to more distant people and finally everyone on earth.
rows.anchor: جرى ذِكْرُ القرابات قبل هذا المشهد فقال: {وَلاَ يَسْأَلُ حَمِيمٌ حَمِيماً}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following description of human anxiety and panic explains why the criminal starts by offering those nearest and dearest to him.
rows.anchor: ذكر بعد هذه الآيات أن الإنسان {خُلِقَ هَلُوعاً * إِذَا مَسَّهُ الشر جَزُوعاً * وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ الخير مَنُوعاً}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Starting with the closest relatives shows that the punishment is beyond imagining and leaves no room for bargaining.
rows.anchor: يدل على أن العذاب فوق التصور، وهولُهُ أبعدُ من الخيال بحيث جعله يبدأ بأقرب الناس إليه

rows.speaker: أنوار التنزيل
rows.claim: Anwār al-Tanzīl explains that each criminal becomes so absorbed in himself that he wishes to ransom himself with his nearest and dearest, rather than care about their welfare.
rows.anchor: جاء في (أنوار التنزيل) في قوله تعالى: {يَوَدُ المجرم لَوْ يَفْتَدِي مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمِئِذٍ بِبَنِيهِ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ransom list proceeds through children, wife, brother, clan, and all earth’s people, leaving no one except the person seeking ransom.
rows.anchor: فرتَّبهن ترتيباً آخر مبتدئاً بالأبناء فالزوجة فالأخ فالفصيلة، وفيهم الأبوان ثم انتهى بأهل الأرض أجمعين، فلا يبقى أحد غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qāriʿah repeats its name to magnify the terror, so mountains as fluffed wool are more frightening than wool without the added image of fluffing.
rows.anchor: قال في سورة القارعة: {القارعة * مَا القارعة * وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا القارعة} فكرر ذِكْرَها وعظمها وهولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Maʿārij calls the punishment inevitable and undeterred, like weight settling on wool; al-Qāriʿah’s repeated striking fluffs the wool, fitting its added descriptor.
rows.anchor: ذكر في سورة المعارج أن العذاب (واقع) وأنه ليس له دافع {سَأَلَ سَآئِلٌ بِعَذَابٍ وَاقِعٍ * لِّلْكَافِرِينَ لَيْسَ لَهُ دَافِعٌ} ووقوع الثقل على الصوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qāriʿah’s expanded description supports the extra detail, whereas al-Maʿārij gives a brief account and mentions only the day lasting fifty thousand years.
rows.anchor: التوسع والتفصيل في ذكر القارعة حسّن ذِكْرَ الزيادةِ والتفصيل فيها، بخلاف الإجمال في سورة المعارج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording fits each passage’s cadence: المنفوش echoes المبثوث in al-Qāriʿah, while العهن pairs with المهل in al-Maʿārij.
rows.anchor: فناسبت كلمة (المنفوش) كلمة (المبثوث)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qāriʿah’s hot fire suits wool fluffed by heat melting mountains; al-Maʿārij instead describes a blaze that strips skin.
rows.anchor: ناسب ذكر العهن المنفوش أيضاً قوله في آخر السورة {نَارٌ حَامِيَةٌ} لأن النار الحامية هي التي تُذِيبُ الجبالَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿādūn means transgressors; the emphatic they are the transgressors marks them as consummate offenders because unlawful sex harms themselves, family, descendants, and society.
rows.anchor: و {العادون} هم المعتدون، ومعنى الآية: أن هؤلاء هم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Constantly performing prayer means not letting distractions interrupt it; guarding prayer means observing its conditions and completing its obligations, sunnahs, and remembrances.
rows.anchor: فإن معنى الدوام هو أن لا ينشغل عنها بشيء من الشواغل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guarding prayer connects to the earlier description of hoarding: one stores wealth in a container to preserve it, and prayer deserves preservation even more.
rows.anchor: وارتباط هذه الآية بما قبلها واضح فهي مرتبطة بقوله: {وَجَمَعَ فأوعى} ذلك أن القصد من جعل المال في وعاء، هو المحافظة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maintaining prayer through ease, hardship, illness, and health cures human panic; it requires patience and willingness to forgo profit, as shown by the commands in Ṭā Hā and al-Nūr.
rows.anchor: ذلك أن المحافظة عليها تحتاج إلى الصبر الطويل، لذلك قال تعالى: {وَأْمُرْ أَهْلَكَ بالصلاة واصطبر عَلَيْهَا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing the qualities that free people from panic, the passage turns to their reward: honored status in gardens.
rows.anchor: ثم قال بعد ذلك: {أولائك فِي جَنَّاتٍ مُّكْرَمُونَ}

none: Bibliography only; no interpretation or other point about the verse.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He frames the comparison by asking why al-Mu’minūn confirms death with lām while al-Zumar states ميتون without it; this excerpt poses the question but does not answer it.
rows.anchor: لِمَ قال في آيةِ (المؤمنون) : {لَمَيِّتُونَ} باللام، وقال في الزمر: {مَّيِّتُونَ} من دون لام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect normally denotes the present and conflicts with the future phrase on Resurrection Day; he treats 16:124 as an exception that may preserve present meaning through an implied temporal governor, so this is a tendency, not a rule.
rows.anchor: المضارع للحال غالباً، فلا تجامع يوم القيامة، لأن إعمال (تبعثون) في الظرف المستقبل تخلصه للاستقبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the stronger confirmation of death by إن and lām, compared with resurrection affirmed by إن alone, has several causes and suits al-Mu’minūn’s atmosphere.
rows.anchor: مما تقدم يتضح أن تأكيد الموت بإنَّ واللام، وتأكيد البعث بإنّ وحدها له أكثر من سبب يدعو إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each ending suits its local context and surah: resurrection completes al-Mu’minūn’s account of human life from creation through development to its end, while al-Zumar ends with dispute.
rows.anchor: فإنَّ آية (المؤمنون) وقعت في سياق بَدْءِ خَلْقِ الإنسان وتطوره إلى منتهاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He expects later generations and specialists in law and medicine to uncover further signs, including precise Qur’anic legal and technical word choices beyond his own literary observations.
rows.anchor: وسيجد فيه أجيالُ المستقبل من ملامح الإعجاز وإشاراته ما لم يخطر لنا على بال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the Qur’anic stages of fetal development match findings established only in the modern era and notes that this led some foreign scientists to declare Islam.
rows.anchor: ما ذكره القرآن من مراحل تطور الجنين في الرحم هي التي انتهى إليها العلمُ مما لم يكنْ معروفاً قبل هذا العصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term al-ʿalaqah is scientifically precise because the developing embryo at this stage resembles a leech.
rows.anchor: فاختيار التعبير بـ (العلقة) اختيارٌ له دلالته، فإن المخلوق في هذه المرحلة أشبه شيء بالعلقة

rows.speaker: كتب التفسير
rows.claim: The tafsir books define a muḍghah as a piece of flesh about the size a person can chew.
rows.anchor: فالمضغة كما قرأنا في كتب التفسير، هي القطعة من اللحم قدر ما يمضغ الماضغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He adds that muḍghah specifically means flesh chewed by teeth; the embryo resembles such a piece, making the Qur’anic word choice scientifically precise.
rows.anchor: ذلك أن (المضغة) هي قطعة اللحم الممضوغة أي التي مضغتها الأسنان، وقد أثبت العلمُ الحديث أن الجنين في هذه المرحلة ليس قطعة لحم عادية
